title: Filtering Rows With WHERE
summary: Keep only the rows you want with comparisons and AND, OR, and NOT.
intro: Most questions about a table are about some of its rows: the long books, the books on the shelf, the ones from before 1950. `WHERE` picks those rows out.
setup:
CREATE TABLE books (
    id integer PRIMARY KEY,
    title text,
    author text,
    genre text,
    pages integer,
    published integer,
    available boolean
);

INSERT INTO books (id, title, author, genre, pages, published, available) VALUES
    (1, 'The Hobbit', 'J.R.R. Tolkien', 'Fantasy', 310, 1937, true),
    (2, 'Dune', 'Frank Herbert', 'Science Fiction', 412, 1965, false),
    (3, 'The Hound of the Baskervilles', 'Arthur Conan Doyle', 'Mystery', 256, 1902, true),
    (4, 'Neuromancer', 'William Gibson', 'Science Fiction', 271, 1984, true),
    (5, 'A Wizard of Earthsea', 'Ursula K. Le Guin', 'Fantasy', 183, 1968, false),
    (6, 'Pride and Prejudice', 'Jane Austen', 'Classic', 432, 1813, true),
    (7, 'The Name of the Wind', 'Patrick Rothfuss', 'Fantasy', 662, 2007, false),
    (8, 'Gone Girl', 'Gillian Flynn', 'Mystery', 419, 2012, true);

steps.title: Comparisons
steps.body:
`WHERE` keeps only the rows whose condition is true. It goes after `FROM` and before `ORDER BY`. Every program in this lesson uses a `books` table:

```sql harness
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS books CASCADE;
{{code}}
```

```sql
CREATE TABLE books (
    id integer PRIMARY KEY,
    title text,
    author text,
    genre text,         -- 'Fantasy', 'Science Fiction', 'Mystery', 'Classic'
    pages integer,
    published integer,  -- the year, like 1965
    available boolean
);
```

It holds 8 books, such as The Hobbit (Fantasy, 310 pages, 1937, available) and Dune (Science Fiction, 412 pages, 1965, not available).

The comparison operators are `=`, `<>` (not equal, `!=` works too), `<`, `>`, `<=` and `>=`. Equality is a single `=`, not `==`. They work on numbers, text, and booleans:

```sql
SELECT title FROM books WHERE published >= 2000 ORDER BY id;
SELECT title FROM books WHERE genre <> 'Mystery' ORDER BY id;
SELECT title FROM books WHERE available = false ORDER BY id;
```

Text compares case sensitively, so `genre = 'fantasy'` matches nothing. `<` and `>` compare text in sort order, so `title < 'M'` keeps titles that sort before M, like Dune. Text goes in single quotes. Double quotes mean a column name, so `genre = "Fantasy"` stops with this error:

```text
ERROR:  column "Fantasy" does not exist
```

Try it in the editor to see the error.

Watch the edges: `published < 1950` leaves out a book from 1950, while `<=` keeps it.

example.title: Long books and fantasy
example.prompt: List the books with more than 300 pages, then the Fantasy books with their authors.
example.code:
SELECT title, pages
FROM books
WHERE pages > 300
ORDER BY id;

SELECT title, author
FROM books
WHERE genre = 'Fantasy'
ORDER BY id;
example.output:
title         | pages
----------------------+-------
 The Hobbit           |   310
 Dune                 |   412
 Pride and Prejudice  |   432
 The Name of the Wind |   662
 Gone Girl            |   419
(5 rows)

        title         |      author
----------------------+-------------------
 The Hobbit           | J.R.R. Tolkien
 A Wizard of Earthsea | Ursula K. Le Guin
 The Name of the Wind | Patrick Rothfuss
(3 rows)
example.explanation: Each query checks its condition on every row and keeps the rows where it is true. `pages > 300` compares numbers, so The Hobbit with 310 pages stays. `genre = 'Fantasy'` compares text exactly. `ORDER BY id` still comes last and sorts only the rows that survived.

practice.title: Old books and mysteries
practice.prompt:
List the older books in the library, then its mysteries.

1. Select `title` and `published` from `books` for the books published before 1950. A book from exactly 1950 does not count.
2. Sort that result by `id`.
3. Then select `title` and `author` for the books whose genre is `Mystery`, sorted by `id`.

The table holds the 8 books described in this part: The Hobbit (1937), The Hound of the Baskervilles (1902, Mystery), Pride and Prejudice (1813), Gone Girl (2012, Mystery), and four books published after 1950.

Expected output:

```text
             title             | published
-------------------------------+-----------
 The Hobbit                    |      1937
 The Hound of the Baskervilles |      1902
 Pride and Prejudice           |      1813
(3 rows)

             title             |       author
-------------------------------+--------------------
 The Hound of the Baskervilles | Arthur Conan Doyle
 Gone Girl                     | Gillian Flynn
(2 rows)
```
practice.starter:
-- TODO: keep only the books published before 1950
SELECT title, published
FROM books
ORDER BY id;

-- TODO: keep only the Mystery books
SELECT title, author
FROM books
ORDER BY id;
practice.solution:
SELECT title, published
FROM books
WHERE published < 1950
ORDER BY id;

SELECT title, author
FROM books
WHERE genre = 'Mystery'
ORDER BY id;

tests.output:
title             | published
-------------------------------+-----------
 The Hobbit                    |      1937
 The Hound of the Baskervilles |      1902
 Pride and Prejudice           |      1813
(3 rows)

             title             |       author
-------------------------------+--------------------
 The Hound of the Baskervilles | Arthur Conan Doyle
 Gone Girl                     | Gillian Flynn
(2 rows)

title             | published
-------------------------------+-----------
 The Hobbit                    |      1937
 The Hound of the Baskervilles |      1902
 Pride and Prejudice           |      1813
 Nineteen Eighty-Four          |      1949
 The Big Sleep                 |      1939
(5 rows)

     title     |      author
---------------+------------------
 Gone Girl     | Gillian Flynn
 The Big Sleep | Raymond Chandler
(2 rows)

tests.stdin:
DELETE FROM books WHERE published < 1950;
DELETE FROM books WHERE genre = 'Mystery';
tests.output:
title | published
-------+-----------
(0 rows)

 title | author
-------+--------
(0 rows)

hints: Add a `WHERE` line between `FROM` and `ORDER BY` in each query.
Use `<` for strictly before, and put the text `'Mystery'` in single quotes.

steps.title: Combining conditions
steps.body:
Join conditions with `AND` (both must be true) and `OR` (at least one must be true). `NOT` flips a condition.

```sql
SELECT title FROM books WHERE genre = 'Fantasy' AND pages < 300 ORDER BY id;
SELECT title FROM books WHERE genre = 'Mystery' OR genre = 'Classic' ORDER BY id;
SELECT title FROM books WHERE NOT genre = 'Fantasy' ORDER BY id;
```

Comparisons are worked out first, so `NOT genre = 'Fantasy'` flips the whole comparison.

A boolean column is already true or false, so it works as a condition on its own. Write `WHERE available` instead of `WHERE available = true`, and `WHERE NOT available` instead of `WHERE available = false`.

Among the three, `NOT` binds tightest, then `AND`, then `OR`. So without parentheses this condition:

```sql harness
SELECT title, genre, available
FROM books
{{code}}
ORDER BY id;
```

```sql
WHERE available AND genre = 'Fantasy' OR genre = 'Science Fiction'
```

means `(available AND genre = 'Fantasy') OR genre = 'Science Fiction'`, which lets in every Science Fiction book, available or not. Put parentheses around the `OR` part whenever you mix `AND` and `OR`. They make the grouping you mean explicit, and they cost nothing.

example.title: Available fantasy or sci-fi
example.prompt: List the available books that are Fantasy or Science Fiction, then run the same query without parentheses to see the difference.
example.code:
SELECT title, genre
FROM books
WHERE available AND (genre = 'Fantasy' OR genre = 'Science Fiction')
ORDER BY id;

SELECT title, genre
FROM books
WHERE available AND genre = 'Fantasy' OR genre = 'Science Fiction'
ORDER BY id;
example.output:
title    |      genre
-------------+-----------------
 The Hobbit  | Fantasy
 Neuromancer | Science Fiction
(2 rows)

    title    |      genre
-------------+-----------------
 The Hobbit  | Fantasy
 Dune        | Science Fiction
 Neuromancer | Science Fiction
(3 rows)
example.explanation: In the first query the parentheses make the genre test one unit, and `available` must hold as well, so only The Hobbit and Neuromancer pass. In the second query `AND` runs first, so Dune gets in through `OR genre = 'Science Fiction'` even though it is not available.

practice.title: Checked out short or new books
practice.prompt:
Find the checked out books that are either short or recent.

1. Select `title`, `pages`, and `published` from `books`.
2. Keep the books that are not available and that have fewer than 200 pages or were published after 2000. A book from exactly 2000 does not count as after 2000.
3. Use `NOT` on the boolean column and parentheses around the `OR` part.
4. Sort by `id`.

The table holds 8 books. Three are not available: Dune (412 pages, 1965), A Wizard of Earthsea (183 pages, 1968), and The Name of the Wind (662 pages, 2007). Gone Girl (2012) is new but available.

Expected output:

```text
        title         | pages | published
----------------------+-------+-----------
 A Wizard of Earthsea |   183 |      1968
 The Name of the Wind |   662 |      2007
(2 rows)
```
practice.starter:
-- TODO: keep books that are not available and are short (under 200 pages) or new (after 2000)
SELECT title, pages, published
FROM books
ORDER BY id;
practice.solution:
SELECT title, pages, published
FROM books
WHERE NOT available AND (pages < 200 OR published > 2000)
ORDER BY id;

tests.output:
title         | pages | published
----------------------+-------+-----------
 A Wizard of Earthsea |   183 |      1968
 The Name of the Wind |   662 |      2007
(2 rows)

title         | pages | published
----------------------+-------+-----------
 A Wizard of Earthsea |   183 |      1968
 The Name of the Wind |   662 |      2007
 Gone Girl            |   419 |      2012
 Animal Farm          |   112 |      1945
(4 rows)

title         | pages | published
----------------------+-------+-----------
 A Wizard of Earthsea |   183 |      1968
(1 row)

hints: `NOT available` keeps the books that are checked out.
Without parentheses `AND` runs before `OR`, so wrap the page test and the year test together in parentheses.

recap:
- `WHERE condition` keeps the rows where the condition is true. It goes after `FROM` and before `ORDER BY`.
- Compare with `=`, `<>` or `!=`, `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=`. Equality is one `=`.
- Text goes in single quotes and compares case sensitively.
- `AND` needs both sides, `OR` needs one, `NOT` flips a condition.
- A boolean column is a condition on its own: `WHERE available`, `WHERE NOT available`.
- `AND` runs before `OR`, so wrap the `OR` part in parentheses when you mix them.
